## Historical audit — S0299

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/historical_r1_C2_start/development/commons_31294395/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines in this file; observations were not split across chunks.

**Goal:** Reconstruct a single indoor photograph as separate SceneAct/Blender objects, matching viewpoint, framing, geometry and materials. The student inferred a furnished bedroom; that inventory is a model interpretation, not independent inspection of the image (line 1, `model_request`; line 3, H `model_response`).

| Stage | Observed evidence |
|---|---|
| Initial build | H produced named architecture, two windows, pictures, furniture, folding screen, bed, armchair, small chair and rugs. Bed and chair have named component meshes grouped into assets; this establishes emitted hierarchy, not physical connection or correct occlusion. Code assigns colors, procedural noise wallpaper, a camera and two area lights (lines 3–4, `model_response`/`execute`). |
| First validation and revision | Step 1 built and rendered successfully; the runner returned the render to H (lines 6–11). H described the view as too distant, corner too far right, furniture too small, bed sideways and chair too round. Step 2 moved the camera, extended walls, rotated bed and chair, and added a nightstand; these are executed changes, not verified corrections (lines 13–14). |
| Second revision | Step 2 also built and rendered successfully and its image was supplied to H (lines 16–21). H reported excessive floor and ceiling, small bed/windows, misplaced corner and chair pose. Step 3 enlarged and moved the bed, further rotated the chair, adjusted camera/lens, colors and lighting, and executed the full program (lines 23–24). |
| Final result | Step 3 build and render returned zero and `ok: true`; step 3 was selected (lines 26–30). There is no subsequent H review or visible formal quality evaluation. |

**Teacher and autonomy.** No separate teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update or student receipt is visible. The initial system instructions and runner’s generic compare-or-finish prompts were received; the subsequent specific diagnoses and revisions are H’s own. The session records show no independent tool calls within H’s sessions, while the outer runner executed the three programs (lines 2, 11–12, 21–22). Thus the trace shows autonomous iterative revision using supplied renders, not demonstrated adoption of teacher feedback.

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Technical build/render success is established, but **reconstruction correctness is unknown**, not formal success or demonstrated algorithm failure. Neither the reference nor rendered pixels are visible in this audit. Multiple objects and materials are evidenced by code, but actual appearance, texture fidelity, part contact, object pose, camera alignment, illumination and occlusion remain unverified. H’s comparisons are reports, not independent visual or geometric verification; whether the last camera and pose changes improved the match is an unresolved hypothesis.

**Lessons.** Transferable process evidence is the separation of a runnable render from visual correctness and the use of render feedback to motivate editable scene revisions. The particular bedroom inventory, rotations and camera values are task-specific; this trace does not establish that they generalize or that the final choices were correct.
